summary:
Our team is taking on the Space Mission Design Game challenge. We aim to design an engaging game in which the player pilots a spacecraft towards an astronomical body and attempts a successful landing. 

The game challenges the player to choose the right time, direction and velocity to launch from the earth and make a successful rendez-vous with the moon.

The trajectory calculations consider the spinning of the earth, the rotation of the moon around the earth, the initial velocity and direction of the spacecraft and the effect of gravity on the spacecraft.
details:
What does it do?

This game is a simulation of the trajectory of a spacecraft as it launches from earth on missions to the moon, mars and other planets in the solar system.

How does it work?

The player uses SpaceCoin to buy rockets. They set the parameters of mass, thrust and direction, and then click launch to commence the flight simulation. If the flight is successful, the player wins SpaceCoin and can continue to a more demanding flight.

What benefits does it have?

The player learns about the difficulties of frames or reference and rotating bodies when considering a rocket launch. They have to balance the need for greater thrust for more massive spacecraft. The gameplay is intended to engage the player so that they continue launching and learn about the nature of spaceflight in terms of gravity and trajectory.

What coding languages or software did you use to develop your project?

The UI was initially coded in python, using pygame, and then re-coded in C# for implementation in Unity Game Engine. The simulation was run in Unity. The files were shared on GitHub.

What factors did your team consider?

We considered the following factors:

* Will the simulation be realistic?

* Will the game be engaging?

* Will the player learn about trajectories?

* How do we simplify the project so that we can make something that works?
